text.p: Whirlpool Corp., the world's largest appliance maker, Wednesday reported a 21 percent rise in profits for the first quarter, thanks to better results in North America and Latin America.

The Benton Harbour, Mich.-based company said it earned $46 million, or 62 cents a share, on sales of $2.03 billion, up from year-ago earnings of $38 million, or 50 cents a share, on sales of $2.05 billion.
The earnings slightly exceeded Wall Street's expectations for per share income of 58 cents. Whirlpool's stock rose 37.5 cents to $46.125 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
"Overall, we're pleased with the quarter and with the progress it represents toward our full-year goals," said Chairman David Whitwam.

"Our North and Latin American businesses again put up outstanding numbers, and European and Asian results were in line with our interim expectations for what will be meaningful operating improvement through this year," he said.
Whirlpool said its shipments in North America were down slightly, but lower material costs boosted its profit margins.

Whirlpool said North America full-year 1997 industry volumes are expected to be down slightly from record levels in 1996 mainly due to carryover air-conditioner inventories, which are higher than usual.
In 1996, Whirlpool's earnings, excluding a restructuring charge, fell 16 percent from 1995, to $175 million, or $2.33 per share.

Whitman told the company's annual meeting on Tuesday that "results from a poor European market were unsatisfactory, but bottomed out in the second quarter (of 1996) and have trended upward through the first quarter of 1997."
